svg.aria-label: Development. $ Mini/Scripts/engine # once: fetch the Oh-my-pi the build takes in $ cd Mini && cargo test # offline unit tests; live ones are ignored $ cargo build # local debug binary $ cargo tauri build # app bundle, no installation $ python3 -m unittest discover -s Mini/Bench # the browser link's bench, its checkers Use cargo tauri, not bunx tauri: the latter names a different npm package. cargo test -- --ignored is the harness check: live tests on the carried Oh-my-pi with a stand-in provider, one of which reaches a real provider with a dummy key. With them runs the key check, which opens the box for a few seconds, signs in with a marked dummy key and searches Null's log and settings for it, and the box check: about thirty runs of the real app, each one thing a person does in the box, on folders of their own with the stand-in provider. Those take the keyboard for some minutes, so leave the Mac alone and unlocked meanwhile. NULL_MINI_ENGINE=<path> runs the harness check on another Oh-my-pi, and Mini/Scripts/engine --to <version> moves Null to that version only if it passes. NULL_MINI_CHROME=<Chrome for Testing> lets one question load Null's copy of the browser link's extension in a Chrome of its own. Repository CI runs all three on a Mac runner whenever Mini/ changes. Mini/Bench/ measures the browser link on made-up signed-in sites; python3 Mini/Bench/bench.py check proves, with no model, that its runs cannot reach your own Chrome.
